title: We built an RTS with AI assistance. The supply trucks taught us what our tests were missing.
author: Key_Art_9961
selftext:
We’re Knowhubs, the developers of Battlegroup Sea Lines. We used AI to help write the Godot code and ChatGPT Images for the menu illustration and button surfaces. One of the most revealing tests was simply starting a skirmish with a mouse. A supply truck could complete its route once it had an order, but a starting truck could sit there waiting for the player to give it one. That felt wrong the moment we played.



We changed the opening so that, once you deploy the mobile HQ, the trucks collect from supplies you’ve actually discovered and can reach. You can still give a truck a manual order. In our release playtest they delivered 520 supplies while we placed a barracks, changed its rally point and trained two squads.



For anyone building games with AI-assisted code, what do you put in the very first minute of a human playtest? Ours is now “deploy the HQ and give the trucks no orders.” It catches a different problem from asking whether a truck can follow a route.



The Windows Early Access build is free, with optional tips. Start with Coastal Skirmish if you want to try the opening. [https://knowhubs.itch.io/battlegroup-sea-lines](https://knowhubs.itch.io/battlegroup-sea-lines)
